events.title: La Salle Claims the Mississippi Basin for France
events.description: After canoeing down the Mississippi River, French explorer René-Robert Cavelier de La Salle reached its mouth at the Gulf of Mexico. He claimed the whole river basin for King Louis XIV and named it Louisiana.
events.significance: The claim gave France a vast North American territory. That territory was later sold to the United States in the 1803 Louisiana Purchase.

events.title: Lee Surrenders at Appomattox
events.description: Confederate General Robert E. Lee surrendered the Army of Northern Virginia to Union General Ulysses S. Grant at Appomattox Court House, Virginia.
events.significance: The surrender effectively ended the American Civil War. It was a decisive step toward the war's conclusion and the preservation of the Union.

events.title: Marian Anderson Sings at the Lincoln Memorial
events.description: The Daughters of the American Revolution refused to let contralto Marian Anderson perform at Constitution Hall. She gave an Easter Sunday concert at the Lincoln Memorial instead, before a crowd of about 75,000.
events.significance: The concert became a landmark moment in the struggle against racial discrimination in America. It showed how art could challenge segregation.

events.title: Bataan Surrenders to Japanese Forces
events.description: About 75,000 American and Filipino troops on the Bataan Peninsula surrendered to Japanese forces during World War II. The surrender was followed by the Bataan Death March.
events.significance: It was one of the largest surrenders in American military history. The brutal march that followed became a lasting symbol of wartime suffering.
